It therefore never throws when posthog is not loaded — safe for every form onSuccess caller and for the OnboardingProfile mount effect. identifyUser control flow is unchanged by the feature: the diff (git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9) added only two window.logger calls — one inside the pre-existing `if (!ph)` block before its `return` (skip path), one on the fire path before `ph.identify(...)`. The early-return semantics on `!ph` are preserved; no behavioral change beyond logging. window.logger is a defined global (app/javascript/shared/logger.ts), so the added log lines cannot throw. OnboardingProfile.tsx: the mount effect (lines 28-35) fires exactly one plain trackEvent with no properties, and the two event names match SPEC §5.6/D18 exactly (organization_owner_email_verified / invited_user_email_verified). Verified isNewOwner can never be undefined -> wrong branch: wasInvited (line 17) is a strict boolean (undefined?.role === string OR-chain yields false when currentOrganizationUser is absent); isNewOwner = !wasInvited && currentUser?.createdVia !== 'created_via_invite' — optional-chaining on an absent currentUser yields `undefined !== 'created_via_invite'` = true, so isNewOwner is always a concrete boolean and `if (isNewOwner)` always selects a real branch. The wasInvited/isNewOwner computation (lines 16-18) is NOT in the feature delta — it pre-exists and D18 explicitly sanctions reusing it. final_message: Both files are sound. trackEvent guards against missing posthog — getPosthog() returns null when !posthog.__loaded, and trackEvent's `if (!ph)` logs-and-returns before touching ph.capture, so it never throws for any form onSuccess caller. identifyUser's control flow is unchanged; the feature added only window.logger lines and preserved the early return on !ph. In OnboardingProfile, isNewOwner is always a concrete boolean (never undefined), the mount effect only runs after the AppAuthRouter guard guarantees currentUser is loaded, and currentOrganizationUser is derived synchronously from it — so the correct event fires for every population per D18. No findings.
